message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command to launch the Docker Engine itself – it only starts an existing container.  
To bring the Docker service up on Windows you need to start the *service* that runs the Docker daemon.

### Start the Docker service (requires Administrator)

```powershell
# PowerShell
Start-Service -Name com.docker.service
```

or

```cmd
:: Command Prompt
net start com.docker.service
```

If you’re using Docker Desktop, you can also launch the GUI directly:

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"
```

> **Tip:**  
> • Make sure you run the shell as Administrator.  
> • If you’re using Docker Machine, you would use `docker-machine start <machine-name>` instead.  

Once the service is running, you can then use `docker start <container-id>` to start individual containers.
